extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DOD contracting officers, acquisition professionals, and policymakers implementing OMB Circular A-76 (CITA program)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for contracting officers to implement OMB Circular No. A-76 via the DOD Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITA) program, covering assessment, acquisition planning, contracting, award, and administration phases. Focuses on Navy field procurement system issues, responsibilities, and procedural standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial or Industrial Type Activity (CITA) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal Executive Agency that provides a product or service obtainable from a private commercial source; the activity can be identified with an organization or a type of work but must be (1) separable from other functions so as to be suitable for performance either in-house or by contract; and (2) a regularly needed activity of an operational nature, not a one-time activity of short duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these two tests (separability and regularly needed operational nature) to determine whether an activity falls under A-76/CITA; a CITA may be designated a C/I activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial or Industrial Type Activity Support Service (CITASS) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The services provided as a result of or in conjunction with the operation of a CITA; CITA support services (CITASS) are non-personal and the CITA program contemplates contracting-out the entire function for a sustained period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish CITASS from Contractor Support Services (CSS): CITASS contemplates full-function sustained contracting (flows directly from A-76), while CSS are short-term, task-specific support obtained via normal acquisition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparison (Comparative Cost Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An accurate determination of whether it is more economical to acquire needed products or services from the private sector or from an existing or proposed Government commercial or industrial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the A-76 Cost Comparison Handbook and Transmittal Memorandum No.4 (March 1979); use specified methodologies (e.g., incremental costing), include appropriate benefit/insurance/retirement rates, and ensure equitable, consistent comparisons between in-house and contractor costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost margins established by OMB Circular A-76 that must be exceeded before performing a 'new-start' in-house and before converting an in-house activity to contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the prescribed differential thresholds in analyzing whether to start in-house work or convert to contract performance; these are policy-triggering margins rather than mere estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Function (criteria for mandatory in-house performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government function is one which must be performed by the Government (in-house) due to a special relationship in executing governmental responsibilities including (1) discretionary application of Government authority, (2) monetary transactions and entitlements, and (3) maintenance of in-house technical core capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one of these criteria applies, the function should remain in-house despite commercial availability; assess national security and core capability considerations carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Start (definition/thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly established Government commercial industrial activity, including a transfer of work from contract to in-house performance; also includes any expansion which would increase capital investment or annual operating costs by 100 percent or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numeric thresholds for capital investment and operating cost increases to determine whether an action qualifies as a new start subject to A-76 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion (definition/thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The modernization, replacement, upgrade, or enlargement of a CITA that involves adding a capital investment of $100,000 or more or increasing annual operations costs by $200,000 or more, provided the increase exceeds 20 percent of the capital investment or annual operating cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the stated dollar and percentage thresholds; consolidation of multiple activities isn't an expansion unless totals exceed thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of availability of commercial sources (Phase I Assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment to determine whether commercial sources exist to provide the product or service required, as part of Phase I of the CITA cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate market availability, capability, and whether equivalent commercial service exists; this is an early gate in the cost-comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple functions (assessment consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of activities that perform multiple functions which may complicate separability and cost-comparison analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and separate functions where possible; address challenges when multiple functions are intertwined (e.g., shared staff, facilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of same functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of consolidating identical or similar functions across activities as part of the assessment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate consolidation effects on cost, efficiency, and whether consolidation constitutes expansion or new start under thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with interested groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications and outreach with stakeholders (Civil Service Commission, unions, contractor associations, Congress, GAO, OMB, OFPP, private industry) during implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent communication to assure equitable implementation and to manage controversy; public review and comment processes are part of policy revision and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and staffing issues (Phase II Planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess organizational structure and staffing needs when planning acquisition for conversion/contracting under CITA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify organizational responsibilities, necessary authorizations, and staffing adjustments required to carry out solicitations, evaluations, and contract administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the impact of CITA implementation on workload across contracting and support offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for changes in workload during transition, including implications for resources and scheduling of other procurement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement administration lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of lead times required for procurement administration as part of acquisition planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for realistic lead times in milestone planning and schedule development to avoid delays in service continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure appropriate contracting authority and delegation are in place for actions under the CITA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and use proper delegations; coordination between NAVSUP, field contracting offices, and other commands is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for contracting personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel must be familiar with procedures and methodologies necessary to carry out A-76/CITA policy (many contracting personnel lacked familiarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted training on cost-comparison methodologies, FAR/DAR provisions, SOW preparation, evaluation, and protest/appeal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task group formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a task group to support planning and execution of CITA studies and acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form multi-disciplinary teams (e.g., contracting, technical, manpower, legal) to prepare cost comparisons, SOWs, and milestone schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of typical milestones and schedules for the CITA program (milestone planning is covered in the study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create explicit milestone charts (pre-solicitation, solicitation, award, conversion phases) to manage the process and track issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of a clear, complete Statement of Work as a key planning element in Phase II acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW must define requirements unambiguously to support fair competition and accurate offers; SOW quality affects evaluation and contract administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer's responsibility for maintaining the integrity of the overall acquisition process in service contracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard fairness, equitable treatment, and adherence to policy; avoid actions that bias comparisons or the procurement outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation: Defense Acquisition Regulation / Contract Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate DAR/DFARS/FAR contract clauses in solicitations supporting the CITA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clauses reflect applicable requirements (labor laws, service contract provisions, firm-cost concepts) and are consistent with policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation: Sources of supply—set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of set-asides (e.g., small business, 8(a)) and sources of supply during pre-solicitation planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate small business and socioeconomic programs consistent with acquisition strategy and legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation: Solicitation methodologies and contract types
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of solicitation procedures and contract types (e.g., firm bid/offer, firm-fixed-price) in support of CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods that align with requirement risk, desired competition, and cost-comparison implications (NAVSUP instructions discuss firm bid/offer usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation: Options and the Cost Comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of contract options and their interaction with the cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze options' effects on comparative economics; options may complicate the government in-house vs. contract cost calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/Evaluation: Pre-bid/Pre-proposal conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences as part of solicitation/evaluation cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conferences to clarify SOW, evaluation criteria, and procedural issues; document attendees and issues raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/Evaluation: Negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiation practices during evaluation of offers as a formal evaluative step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow negotiation rules to preserve fairness; negotiations must not reveal proprietary information or unfairly advantage some offerors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/Evaluation: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure adequate competition in procurements supporting CITA conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote full and open competition where appropriate; document justifications if competition is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/Evaluation: Evaluation of low bid/offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation procedures for low bids/offers (how low bid is assessed relative to government in-house estimate and factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare low offers to government in-house costs, apply evaluation factors, and verify that low bid meets requirements and terms of SOW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award: Evaluation/Award Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to be used in award decisions (technical, price, past performance, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and weight factors in solicitation; apply them consistently during evaluation to support award rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award: Late submission of Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for handling late submission of the government in-house cost estimate during competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear timing rules for release/submission of government estimates; late submission handling affects fairness and post-award challenge risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award: Revealing the Government In-house Cost Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and procedures regarding whether and when to reveal the government in-house cost estimate to offerors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh transparency against competitive risk; NAVSUP/Navy guidance addresses practices and timing for disclosure and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award: Announcement of Cost Comparison results and public review
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement of results of the cost comparison and provision for public review of the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate public notices and reviews to ensure equitable treatment of parties and transparency as required by policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award: Verification of the Government In-house Cost Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification steps to ensure the in-house cost estimate used in comparisons is accurate and defensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct audits/validation of government estimates prior to relying on them for awards; verification reduces protest/appeal risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals versus Protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between appeals and protests and the appropriate handling of each under the CITA/A-76 processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established legal/administrative channels for protests (e.g., GAO) and appeals; document procedures and timelines to manage disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III Administration (post-award administration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of contracts and conversions after award, as Phase III of the CITA program cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage contract performance, transition of personnel/equipment, verification of contractor compliance, and ongoing oversight to ensure continuity and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Contracting Officer (broad responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer's key role in implementing A-76: reviewing policy implementation, establishing frameworks, identifying problem areas, and maintaining integrity and equitable implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers must monitor policy development, apply cost-comparison methodology, coordinate with stakeholders, ensure equitable treatment, and address organizational/procedural impediments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and scope limitations (R&D, GOCO/GOGO, existing in-house capability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain activities (research & development services, many GOCO/GOGO facilities, and existing in-house R&D capabilities) are excluded or deferred from A-76 coverage pending further guidance or statutory limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify exclusions early in scope analysis to avoid misapplying A-76; Congress and transmittal memoranda may impose temporary or permanent exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incremental costing and benefit rate calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological requirement to use appropriate costing methods (e.g., incremental costing) and to apply current rates for health, life insurance, retirement benefits in cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that benefit rate changes (cited swings from 10.7% to 28.7% to 18.1%) materially affect labor cost estimates; follow transmittal memoranda for current rates and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy balancing: reliance on private sector vs. government responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy criterion to rely on private enterprise to the maximum extent possible while recognizing that certain functions must be performed in-house and that relative cost must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a balanced management approach designed to achieve consistent policy implementation, equitable treatment of parties, and improved economy and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory review and evaluation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for developing and reviewing inventories of in-house CITA activities as the basis for cost-comparisons and conversion decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate inventories, update supplemental inventories as required (e.g., FY 78 procedures), and use them to target candidate activities for review.
